items.text: The moment a hive moves is a moment of geodesic parity changing from now-existing here to next-existing, aiming to go in the direction of social moral competency. A hive begins moving as it is-not stable-forming here, and its moving is social abundancing: one same-existing-society opening as two, each going on forward.

items.text: A honey bee colony swarms as it is crowding, its population growing with no room to grow in its nest, its queen's mandibular pheromone thinning through it, open cells for laying running short, with more nectar and pollen and longer days: the old queen goes out with some 50 to 70 percent of the workers, and the parent colony goes on with some 30 to 50 percent, all its brood and several queens developing in their cells, one of them in time going on as its queen. A colony is-not stable-forming here as one, and it opens as two, a social abundancing, each society going on forward.

items.section: 6.7 A school, a flock, a voyaging people, an orienting surface in no self alone
items.text: A swarm's moving begins as 15 or more bees stand at one of the sites together; scouts then scramble through the cluster pressing their vibrating thoraxes against other bees, and each bee's thorax warms to about 35 °C before the swarm lifts off, a five-site test bringing a quorum much more slowly and a lifting off taking almost twice as long. The warming is a build-up and the lifting off a moment: a swarm's parity changing from now-existing in its cluster to next-existing in flight, toward the site its scouts stand at, a whole society warming and going.
